subproblem.title: Coordinate k-planes: dimension k and unit orientations ±e_ι
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and ι : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing, τ_j := e_{ι(j)} (standard basis vectors of ℝ^P) and V := span{τ_j}. Then dim V = k, and there is a k-vector e (a continuous linear functional on k-covectors) with e(α) = α(τ_0, …, τ_{k−1}) for every k-covector α such that both e and −e are unit orientations of V (IsUnitOrientationOf).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (ι : Fin k → Fin P), StrictMono ι → Module.finrank ℝ (Submodule.span ℝ (range (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ) : Fin k → Euclid P))) = k ∧ ∃ e : MultiVector P k, (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) k, e α = α (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ))) ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf e (Submodule.span ℝ (range (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ) : Fin k → Euclid P))) ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (-e) (Submodule.span ℝ (range (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ) : Fin k → Euclid P)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4(i) of the parent proof (“τ := E_p is orthonormal (ι injective), span(range τ) = V_p, and ξ(x)(α) = sign(β_p) α(τ)”), together with “finrank V_p = k” from step 4(iii).

Notation. τ_j := EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) 1 = e_{ι(j)} for j ∈ Fin k, and V := span_ℝ(range τ).

1. τ is orthonormal. The standard basis i ↦ e_i of ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) is orthonormal: it is EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ, an orthonormal basis with basisFun i = single i 1 (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply). ι is strictly increasing, hence injective, so τ = e ∘ ι is orthonormal (Orthonormal.comp).
2. dim V = k. An orthonormal family is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent). So finrank ℝ (span (range τ)) = card (Fin k) = k (finrank_span_eq_card, Fintype.card_fin).
3. The k-vector e.
 - Let ev(α) := α(τ_0, …, τ_{k−1}) for k-covectors α (continuous alternating k-linear maps ℝ^P → ℝ).
 - ev is linear, because addition and scalar multiplication of alternating maps are pointwise.
 - ev is bounded: |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ ∏_j ‖τ_j‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm), and ‖τ_j‖ = |1| = 1 (the norm of a coordinate vector). So |ev(α)| ≤ ‖α‖.
 Hence e := LinearMap.mkContinuous ev 1 is a continuous linear functional, i.e. an element of MultiVector P k, with e(α) = α(τ) for all α. This is the first property of e.
4. IsUnitOrientationOf e V. Take τ itself as the witness. It is orthonormal (step 1), span(range τ) = V by definition, and e(α) = α(τ) for all α, which is the first alternative.
5. IsUnitOrientationOf (−e) V. Take the same witness τ. Negation of continuous linear maps is pointwise, so (−e)(α) = −e(α) = −α(τ) for all α, which is the second alternative. ∎ For k = 0, τ is the empty family, V = {0}, dim V = 0, and e evaluates a 0-covector at the empty tuple; all steps hold verbatim.

subproblem.title: Open lattice faces are disjoint, and their union is flat near each of its points
subproblem.statement: Assume (FG), the exact frozen Lean type of Submission.cmcdtfr_face_geometry. Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let S be a finite set of pairs p = (ι, b) (ι : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing, b ∈ ℤ^P). Write Φ_p(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} (y ∈ ℝ^k), Q₁ := (0,1)^k, F̆_p := Φ_p(Q₁), C := ⋃_{q∈S} F̆_q and V_p := span{e_{ι(j)}}. Then (a) F̆_p ∩ F̆_q = ∅ for distinct p, q ∈ S; and (b) for every p ∈ S and t ∈ Q₁ there is δ > 0 such that, for all z ∈ ℝ^P with |z − Φ_p(t)| < δ, z ∈ C ⟺ z − Φ_p(t) ∈ V_p.

y j) ≤ dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)))) → ∀ (P k : ℕ) (S : Finset ((Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ))), (∀ p ∈ S, StrictMono p.1) → (∀ p ∈ S, ∀ q ∈ S, p ≠ q → Disjoint ((fun y : Euclid k => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) '' {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}) ((fun y : Euclid k => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) '' {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1})) ∧ ∀ p ∈ S, ∀ t : Euclid k, (∀ i, 0 < t i ∧ t i < 1) → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ z : Euclid P, dist z (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, t j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) < δ → (z ∈ ⋃ q ∈ S, (fun y : Euclid k => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) '' {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} ↔ z - subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 4(ii) of the parent proof: the open faces F̆_p are pairwise disjoint, and C ∩ B(x, δ) = Π_p ∩ B(x, δ). The separation and isometry facts come from the antecedent (FG), which is verbatim the frozen type of Submission.cmcdtfr_face_geometry (a resolved dependency of the parent). The parent discharges (FG) with that declaration.

Notation. For p = (ι, b): Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 b + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)} for y ∈ ℝ^k = Euclid k, with e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Also Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 ∀ i}, F̆_p := Φ_p(Q₁), C := ⋃_{q∈S} F̆_q and V_p := span_ℝ{e_{ι(j)} : j ∈ Fin k}. Every p ∈ S has a strictly increasing first component.

0. Facts from (FG), applied at (P, k). For pairs p, q whose first components are strictly increasing:
 (iso) dist(Φ_p y, Φ_p y') = dist(y, y') for all y, y' ∈ ℝ^k;
 (sep) if p ≠ q, y ∈ Q₁ and y' ∈ [0,1]^k, then 1 ≤ dist(Φ_p y, Φ_q y'), or min(y_j, 1 − y_j) ≤ dist(Φ_p y, Φ_q y') for some j.
1. Part (a), disjointness. Let p ≠ q in S, and suppose w ∈ F̆_p ∩ F̆_q, say w = Φ_p(t) = Φ_q(t') with t, t' ∈ Q₁. Since Q₁ ⊆ [0,1]^k, (sep) applies to (p, q, t, t'). But dist(Φ_p t, Φ_q t') = dist(w, w) = 0. The first alternative gives 1 ≤ 0, which is false. The second gives min(t_j, 1 − t_j) ≤ 0 for some j, which is false because 0 < t_j < 1. So F̆_p ∩ F̆_q = ∅.
2. Part (b), choice of δ. Fix p = (ι, b) ∈ S and t ∈ Q₁, and let x := Φ_p(t). Let D be the finite set {1} ∪ {min(t_j, 1 − t_j) : j ∈ Fin k}; it is nonempty because it contains 1. Put δ := min D. Every element of D is positive, so δ > 0. Also δ ≤ 1, and δ ≤ min(t_j, 1 − t_j) for each j. (For k = 0, D = {1} and δ = 1.)
 Now let z ∈ ℝ^P with dist(z, x) < δ. We show z ∈ C ⟺ z − x ∈ V_p.
3. (⇒) Suppose z ∈ C, so z = Φ_q(t') for some q ∈ S and t' ∈ Q₁.
 - If q ≠ p, apply (sep) to (p, q, t, t') (t' ∈ Q₁ ⊆ [0,1]^k). It gives 1 ≤ dist(x, z), or min(t_j, 1 − t_j) ≤ dist(x, z) for some j. But dist(x, z) = dist(z, x) < δ, with δ ≤ 1 and δ ≤ min(t_j, 1 − t_j). Both alternatives are impossible.
 - Hence q = p, and z − x = Φ_p(t') − Φ_p(t) = Σ_j (t'_j − t_j) e_{ι(j)}, because the constant toLp(b) cancels. This is a linear combination of the e_{ι(j)}, so z − x ∈ V_p.
4. (⇐) Suppose z − x ∈ V_p.
 - V_p is spanned by the finite family (e_{ι(j)})_{j ∈ Fin k}, so there is c : Fin k → ℝ with Σ_j c_j e_{ι(j)} = z − x (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun).
 - Let t' := t + toLp(c) ∈ ℝ^k, so t'_j = t_j + c_j. Then Φ_p(t') = toLp(b) + Σ_j t_j e_{ι(j)} + Σ_j c_j e_{ι(j)} = x + (z − x) = z.
 - By (iso), dist(z, x) = dist(Φ_p t', Φ_p t) = dist(t', t) = ‖toLp(c)‖. A coordinate is bounded by the Euclidean norm (PiLp.norm_apply_le), so |c_j| ≤ ‖toLp(c)‖ < δ ≤ min(t_j, 1 − t_j) for each j.
 - Hence t'_j = t_j + c_j > t_j − min(t_j, 1 − t_j) ≥ 0, and t'_j < t_j + min(t_j, 1 − t_j) ≤ 1. So t' ∈ Q₁ and z = Φ_p(t') ∈ F̆_p. Since p ∈ S, z ∈ C.
5. Steps 3 and 4 prove the equivalence for every z with dist(z, x) < δ. This completes part (b). ∎

subproblem.title: A finite disjoint family of oriented rectifiable pieces gives an IMRep with additive action and mass
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, I a type, U ⊆ ℝ^P, S ⊆ I finite, and for p ∈ S: F_p ⊆ ℝ^P Borel with F_p ⊆ U and Hᵏ(F_p) < ∞, the F_p pairwise disjoint, m_p ∈ ℕ positive, ξ_p a k-vector, G_p : ℝ^k → ℝ^P Lipschitz with F_p ⊆ range G_p, and at every x ∈ F_p some subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k C x Q (C := ⋃_{q∈S} F_q) and IsUnitOrientationOf ξ_p Q. Then there is an IMRep R in U of dimension k with R.action(ω) = Σ_{p∈S} m_p ∫_{F_p} ξ_p(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x) for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(U), and R.measure(ℝ^P) = Σ_{p∈S} m_p Hᵏ(F_p).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (I : Type) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : Finset I) (F : I → Set (Euclid P)) (m : I → ℕ) (ξ : I → MultiVector P k) (G : I → Euclid k → Euclid P), (∀ p ∈ S, MeasurableSet (F p)) → (∀ p ∈ S, F p ⊆ U) → (∀ p ∈ S, μHE[k] (F p) ≠ ∞) → (∀ p ∈ S, ∀ q ∈ S, p ≠ q → Disjoint (F p) (F q)) → (∀ p ∈ S, 0 < m p) → (∀ p ∈ S, ∃ K : NNReal, LipschitzWith K (G p)) → (∀ p ∈ S, F p ⊆ range (G p)) → (∀ p ∈ S, ∀ x ∈ F p, ∃ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (⋃ q ∈ S, F q) x Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ p) Q) → ∃ R : IMRep U k, (∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, R.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) = ∑ p ∈ S, (m p : ℝ) * ∫ x in F p, ξ p ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μHE[k]) ∧ R.measure univ = ∑ p ∈ S, (m p : ℝ≥0∞) * μHE[k] (F p)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–6 of the parent proof: the triple (C, θ, ξ), its IMRep fields, the splitting of the action integral over the disjoint pieces, and the computation of R.measure. Here they are stated for an arbitrary finite family of disjoint pieces. The parent instantiates it with the open faces F̆_p = Φ_p((0,1)^k), m_p = |β_p|, ξ_p = ±e_p and G_p = Φ_p.

Notation. Hᵏ := μHE[k] on ℝ^P and C := ⋃_{q∈S} F_q.

1. Carrier. C is Borel, as a finite union of Borel sets (Finset.measurableSet_biUnion). C ⊆ U because each F_q ⊆ U.
2. Uniqueness of the piece. If p, q ∈ S, q ≠ p and x ∈ F_p, then x ∉ F_q, by the disjointness hypothesis.
3. Multiplicity. Let θ(x) := Σ_{q∈S} 1_{F_q}(x) · m_q ∈ ℕ, the sum of the indicators of the F_q with constant values m_q.
 - θ is measurable: each summand is the indicator of a Borel set with a constant value, and ℕ carries the discrete σ-algebra, so the finite sum is measurable (Finset.measurable_sum).
 - By step 2, θ(x) = m_p for x ∈ F_p, p ∈ S.
 - Hence θ > 0 on C, since every point of C lies in some F_p with m_p > 0.
4. Orientation. List S as p₁, …, p_N (S.toList). Define ξ(x) := ξ_{p_i} for the least i with x ∈ F_{p_i}, and ξ(x) := 0 if x ∉ C. Formally, ξ(x) is the right fold over the list of (q, acc) ↦ (if x ∈ F_q then ξ_q else acc), starting from 0.
 - By induction on the list, ξ is strongly measurable: the empty fold is constant, and each step is an if-then-else on a Borel set between a constant and a strongly measurable function (StronglyMeasurable.ite). So ξ is AE-strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞C.
 - By step 2 and induction on the list, ξ(x) = ξ_p whenever x ∈ F_p, p ∈ S: every entry q ≠ p has x ∉ F_q, and the entry p returns ξ_p.
5. Countable rectifiability.
 - With the list p₁, …, p_N, define F_j := G_{p_{j+1}} for j < N, and F_j := the constant map 0 for j ≥ N. Each F_j is Lipschitz, by hypothesis or because it is constant.
 - Every x ∈ C lies in some F_p ⊆ range G_p with p = p_{j+1} for some j < N. So C ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j with M₀ := ∅, and Hᵏ(∅) = 0.
 This is CountablyRectifiable k C.
6. Total weight. The F_p (p ∈ S) are pairwise disjoint and Borel, so ∫⁻_C θ dHᵏ = Σ_{p∈S} ∫⁻_{F_p} θ dHᵏ (lintegral_biUnion_finset). On F_p, θ = m_p (step 3), so ∫⁻_{F_p} θ dHᵏ = m_p Hᵏ(F_p) (setLIntegral_congr_fun, lintegral_const). Hence ∫⁻_C θ dHᵏ = Σ_{p∈S} m_p Hᵏ(F_p), which is finite because every Hᵏ(F_p) < ∞.
7. Local integrability. For compact K ⊆ U, ∫⁻_{C∩K} θ dHᵏ ≤ ∫⁻_C θ dHᵏ < ∞ (lintegral_mono_set).
8. Orients. Let x ∈ C, so x ∈ F_p for some p ∈ S. The hypothesis gives Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k C x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ξ_p Q, and ξ(x) = ξ_p by step 4. So the orients condition holds at every point of C. Since C is Borel, it holds Hᵏ⌞C-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_forall_mem).
9. Steps 1 and 3–8 verify every field of IMRep U k for R := (C, θ, ξ).
10. Action. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(U), and write ω also for the underlying form, which is C^∞ (hence continuous) with compact support. By definition, R.action(ω) = ∫_C θ(x) · ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x).
 - For p ∈ S let g_p(x) := m_p · ξ_p(ω(x)). g_p is continuous, since ξ_p is a continuous linear functional. It has compact support, since ξ_p(0) = 0.
 - Hᵏ⌞F_p is a finite measure, hence finite on compact sets, so g_p is integrable for it (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport).
 - On F_p the integrand θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) equals g_p(x) (steps 3 and 4). Since F_p is Borel, the integrand is integrable on F_p.
 - The Bochner integral is additive over finitely many pairwise disjoint Borel sets (integral_biUnion_finset). So R.action(ω) = Σ_{p∈S} ∫_{F_p} θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ = Σ_{p∈S} ∫_{F_p} m_p ξ_p(ω(x)) dHᵏ = Σ_{p∈S} m_p ∫_{F_p} ξ_p(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x) (setIntegral_congr_fun, integral_const_mul).
11. Mass measure. R.measure = (Hᵏ⌞C).withDensity θ. So R.measure(ℝ^P) = ∫⁻ θ d(Hᵏ⌞C) = ∫⁻_C θ dHᵏ = Σ_{p∈S} m_p Hᵏ(F_p), by withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_univ and step 6. ∎ If S = ∅, then C = ∅, θ = 0 and ξ = 0: every field holds trivially, and both identities read 0 = 0.

subproblem.title: Isometric images: Borel, Hᵏ-measure and change of variables
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let Φ : ℝ^k → ℝ^P be an isometry for the Euclidean metrics and let A ⊆ ℝ^k be Borel. Then Φ(A) is Borel, Hᵏ(Φ(A)) = Lᵏ(A), and ∫_{Φ(A)} h dHᵏ = ∫_A h(Φ(y)) dy for every function h : ℝ^P → ℝ. Here Hᵏ = μHE[k] is the normalized Hausdorff measure, Lᵏ = volume is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^k = Euclid k, and the integrals are Bochner integrals (both 0 when not integrable).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (Φ : Euclid k → Euclid P) (A : Set (Euclid k)), Isometry Φ → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet (Φ '' A) ∧ μHE[k] (Φ '' A) = volume A ∧ ∀ h : Euclid P → ℝ, ∫ x in Φ '' A, h x ∂μHE[k] = ∫ y in A, h (Φ y)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (“Change of variables (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, Φ_p a measurable embedding)”), stated for an arbitrary isometry so that it applies to every face map Φ_p.

Notation. Hᵏ := μHE[k], on ℝ^P or on ℝ^k as indicated; Lᵏ := volume on ℝ^k = Euclid k; μ⌞S := μ.restrict S; Φ_#μ := μ.map Φ.

1. Measurable embedding. ℝ^k is complete and Φ is an isometry, so Φ is a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding). A closed embedding between Borel spaces is a measurable embedding (Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding): Φ is injective and measurable, and it maps Borel sets to Borel sets. In particular Φ(A) is Borel (MeasurableEmbedding.measurableSet_image). This is the first conclusion.
2. Hᵏ = Lᵏ on ℝ^k. By EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume k, the measure μHE[k] on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) equals volume.
3. Measure of the image. Hausdorff measure is invariant under isometries (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), so Hᵏ(Φ(A)) = Hᵏ(A). By step 2, Hᵏ(A) = Lᵏ(A). This is the second conclusion.
4. Push-forward identity: Hᵏ⌞Φ(A) = Φ_#(Lᵏ⌞A), as measures on ℝ^P.
 - Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure gives Φ_#(Hᵏ) = Hᵏ⌞range Φ. Restrict both sides to Φ(A).
 - For a measurable embedding, (Φ_#μ)⌞E = Φ_#(μ⌞Φ⁻¹(E)) for every set E (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map). Take E := Φ(A); injectivity gives Φ⁻¹(Φ(A)) = A. The left side becomes Φ_#(Hᵏ⌞A), which is Φ_#(Lᵏ⌞A) by step 2.
 - On the right, (Hᵏ⌞range Φ)⌞Φ(A) = Hᵏ⌞(Φ(A) ∩ range Φ) by Measure.restrict_restrict (Φ(A) is Borel by step 1). Since Φ(A) ⊆ range Φ, this is Hᵏ⌞Φ(A).
 Equivalently, for every Borel E ⊆ ℝ^P: Φ_#(Lᵏ⌞A)(E) = Lᵏ(A ∩ Φ⁻¹E) = Hᵏ(Φ(A ∩ Φ⁻¹E)) = Hᵏ(Φ(A) ∩ E).
5. Change of variables. Let Φ be a measurable embedding, μ a measure on ℝ^k and h : ℝ^P → ℝ any function. Then ∫ h d(Φ_#μ) = ∫ h∘Φ dμ (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map). No measurability or integrability hypothesis is needed: h is Φ_#μ-integrable if and only if h∘Φ is μ-integrable, and both Bochner integrals are 0 otherwise. Take μ := Lᵏ⌞A and use step 4: ∫_{Φ(A)} h dHᵏ = ∫ h d(Hᵏ⌞Φ(A)) = ∫ h d(Φ_#(Lᵏ⌞A)) = ∫_A h(Φ(y)) dy. This is the third conclusion.
6. Edge cases need nothing extra. For k = 0, ℝ⁰ is a single point, H⁰ = L⁰ is the unit point mass, and the same lemmas apply. If no isometry ℝ^k → ℝ^P exists (k > P), the statement is vacuous. ∎

subproblem.title: A set that coincides with x + V near x has approximate tangent space V at x
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary set, x ∈ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace with dim V = n, and δ > 0. Suppose that for every z ∈ ℝ^P with |z − x| < δ, z ∈ M ⟺ z − x ∈ V. Then V is the approximate tangent space of M at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x V): for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_V f dHⁿ as r → 0⁺, where η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (δ : ℝ), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → 0 < δ → (∀ z : Euclid P, dist z x < δ → (z ∈ M ↔ z - x ∈ V)) → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x V
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4(iii) of the parent proof: the blow-ups of the carrier agree with V_p on B(0, R) for small r, so V_p is the approximate tangent space. Here it is stated for an arbitrary set M and subspace V. It generalizes SimonGMT's hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule (Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter03/Rectifiable.lean), which is the case M = V, x ∈ V.

Notation. η_{x,r}(y) := blowUpMap x r y = r⁻¹ • (y − x); Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P. By definition, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x V means: finrank ℝ V = n, and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), r ↦ ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ tends to ∫_V f dHⁿ along 𝓝[>] 0.

1. finrank ℝ V = n is a hypothesis.
2. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). Its topological support is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ B̄(0, R₀) for some R₀ ∈ ℝ. Put R := max(R₀, 0) + 1, so R > 0 and R > R₀. If |y| ≥ R then y ∉ B̄(0, R₀) ⊇ tsupport f, hence f(y) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). So f vanishes outside the open ball B := B(0, R).
3. Claim: if 0 < r < δ/R (equivalently 0 < r and rR < δ), then B ∩ η_{x,r}(M) = B ∩ V.
 (⊆) Let y ∈ B with y = r⁻¹(z − x) for some z ∈ M. Then z − x = r y, so dist(z, x) = |z − x| = r|y| < rR < δ. By the hypothesis, z ∈ M gives z − x ∈ V. Hence y = r⁻¹(z − x) ∈ V.
 (⊇) Let y ∈ B ∩ V and set z := x + r y. Then z − x = r y ∈ V, since V is a subspace, and dist(z, x) = r|y| < rR < δ. So z ∈ M by the hypothesis. Moreover η_{x,r}(z) = r⁻¹(r y) = y because r ≠ 0. So y ∈ η_{x,r}(M).
4. Localization. For every set S ⊆ ℝ^P, measurable or not, ∫_S f dHⁿ = ∫_{B∩S} f dHⁿ. Indeed, B is Borel, so (Hⁿ⌞S)⌞B = Hⁿ⌞(B ∩ S) (Measure.restrict_restrict). Since f = 0 off B, ∫ f d((Hⁿ⌞S)⌞B) = ∫ f d(Hⁿ⌞S) (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
5. For 0 < r < δ/R, steps 4, 3 and 4 again give
 ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{B∩η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{B∩V} f dHⁿ = ∫_V f dHⁿ.
6. Since δ/R > 0, the interval (0, δ/R) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). So r ↦ ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ is eventually equal along 𝓝[>] 0 to the constant ∫_V f dHⁿ, and hence tends to it (tendsto_const_nhds.congr'). As f was arbitrary, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x V holds. ∎ No measurability of M is used. For n = 0 and V = {0} the argument is identical.

proof_key_steps: tsupport f is compact, so f = 0 outside B(0, R) for some R > 0.
For 0 < r < δ/R, B(0,R) ∩ η_{x,r}(M) = B(0,R) ∩ V: |z − x| = r|η_{x,r}(z)| < δ, then apply the local hypothesis in both directions.
Restricting to the Borel ball does not change ∫ f, so ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ = ∫_V f dHⁿ for all small r.
The map is eventually constant along 𝓝[>]0, which gives the limit; finrank V = n is a hypothesis.
